text: RTI Act 2005, s.6(1): ask for government information by a written or electronic application to the Public Information Officer (PIO) of the public authority, with the prescribed fee (Rs 10 for central authorities; state fees differ). People below the poverty line are exempt from the fee.
RTI Act 2005, s.7(1): the PIO must reply within 30 days of receiving the application; within 48 hours if the information concerns the life or liberty of a person.

RTI Act 2005, s.19: if there is no reply or the reply is unsatisfactory, file a first appeal with the senior officer in the same authority within 30 days; a second appeal to the Information Commission lies within 90 days of the first-appeal decision.
For online/UPI fraud, call the National Cyber Crime Helpline 1930 and report at cybercrime.gov.in as quickly as possible; fast reporting improves the chance of the money being held.

RBI's July 2017 circular on customer protection in unauthorised electronic banking transactions: if reported to the bank within 3 working days, the customer's liability is generally zero where the fault lies with the bank or system; later reporting can mean limited liability per the bank's policy. Check the current circular.

Unpaid salary or withheld full-and-final dues can be raised with the state Labour Department / Labour Commissioner. Which wage law applies (Payment of Wages Act 1936 or the Code on Wages 2019) depends on notification status and the worker's category; verify.
Limitation Act 1963: a civil suit to recover money generally has to be filed within 3 years from when the amount fell due.
For provident-fund (PF) problems such as employer not depositing PF, use the EPFO grievance portal (EPFiGMS); keep payslips showing PF deductions.
Legal Services Authorities Act 1987: free legal aid is available to eligible people through District/State Legal Services Authorities. NALSA helpline: 15100.
